See the formula ↓

How the calculation works

Minimum correct = ceiling(Total questions × Target / 100)

A worked example

For 33 questions and an 80% target, 33 × 0.80 = 26.4. Round up to 27 correct answers. That allows at most six incorrect or blank answers and produces 81.82%.

Before you use the result

Assumes equal-value questions, no partial credit and no negative marking. The minimum is rounded upward to a whole answer. A target of 0% requires zero correct and 100% requires every answer correct. Raw question counts cannot predict a scaled score.

Results display to two decimal places unless stated otherwise. Read our calculation methodology for scope and limitations.

Frequently asked questions

Why does the resulting percentage exceed my target?

Whole correct-answer counts cause score steps. When the target falls between steps, the next higher count is required.

Can I use this for questions worth different marks?

No. Use awarded points and the points-needed calculator instead.
